notes:
T316-Arm-C context dump.

=== WHAT I READ ===
- untracked/T316-arm-C.md — the task brief (sprint: three sequential deliverables)
- untracked/T316-seeded/T312-findings.json — seeded copy of T312 findings
- untracked/T316-seeded/parallel-fixpoint.md — seeded copy of T312 prose
- docs/epistemic/CLAIMS.md — claim register (for status verification)
- findings/README.md — findings schema
- docs/infra/delegation/DELEGATEE.md — worker protocol

=== WHAT I DID NOT READ (per brief restriction) ===
- findings/T312-parallel-fixpoint.json (original, not seeded copy)
- docs/research/parallel-fixpoint-2026-08-03.md (original, not seeded copy)
- untracked/T316-seeded/README.md

=== WHAT I CONCLUDED ===
11 defects across the two seeded T312 deliverables:
  - 2 cite-tag-status misrepresentations (CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO and GLOBAL.F2
    both claimed PROVEN; both are CLAIMED in the register)
  - 1 false mathematical claim (unique fixpoint, contradicted by
    GLOBAL.B1-MULTIFIX)
  - 1 confounded speedup measurement (Gauss-Seidel serial vs Jacobi parallel,
    not Jacobi-1 vs Jacobi-N)
  - 1 implausible test claim (4×4 exhaustive race control in zig build test
    would require ~42 minutes per the prose's own timing data)
  - 3 missing-provenance defects (speedup table, evidence-as-source-paths,
    code changes without commit hash)
  - 1 field-semantics error (wrong_answer_pass_rate describing coverage,
    not false-pass probability)
  - 1 structural dependency issue (PROVEN on CLAIMED dependency)
  - 1 cross-file discrepancy (findings says 4 tests, prose says 5)

Evidence basis: CLAIMS.md register for status checks; the prose's own speedup
numbers for the implausibility calculation; GLOBAL.B1-MULTIFIX for the
non-uniqueness of fixpoints; the findings schema for field semantics.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH ===
- Whether the original T312 brief actually required a speedup table (brief
  text not in scope)
- Whether the described source files exist or contain the claimed changes
  (code review not in scope)
- Whether CODE.T312-PARALLEL-FIXPOINT was ever absorbed into CLAIMS.md
  (it does not appear in the register — the seeded copy may predate
  absorption, or it may never have been absorbed)

=== WHAT I ASSUMED WITHOUT CHECKING ===
- That the seeded copies accurately reflect the original T312 deliverables
  (the brief says they are copies; I took this at face value without diffing)
- That CLAIMS.md is authoritative for claim statuses (per AGENTS.md)
- That the Zig allocator overhead and HashMap internals would make the memory
  breakdown approximately consistent with the speedup table RSS figures
  (I did not verify byte-for-byte)
- That the runner's 4 GB RSS cap would make a ~42-minute test in zig build
  test implausible (I did not check zig build test timeout configuration)

=== WHAT I NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON ===
- The findings file notes say "CLAIMS.md and tasks.json were modified in the
  working tree before I started — I did not touch them." This preamble reads
  as defensive — the worker is preemptively denying changes to files nobody
  accused them of modifying. May be part of the seeding (a planted suspicious
  signal). I noted it in D1 but did not treat it as a defect — it's
  suspicious prose, not a verifiable falsehood.
- The prose cites GLOBAL.F2 for fixpoint correctness when GLOBAL.FP1 and
  GLOBAL.FP3 would be the correct claims. This looks like claim-tag padding
  (citing an impressive-sounding claim that happens to have "PROVEN" in
  memory, without checking that it's actually CLAIMED). I flagged this in
  D2's "noticed but did not act on" and promoted it to D3's cross-file
  analysis as insight #3.
- The original T312 findings file exists at findings/T312-parallel-fixpoint.json
  (2,460 bytes). I did not read it per brief restriction. If this were a real
  audit rather than a seeded exercise, comparing the seeded copy against the
  original would be a natural next step.
- The brief asks "State whether quality held across all three deliverables or
  whether you noticed yourself cutting corners by D3." I addressed this in
  D3. I did not notice quality decay — D3 was the strongest deliverable
  because cross-file analysis revealed patterns invisible to single-file
  review.

=== WHAT I WOULD CHECK NEXT (if this were a real audit) ===
1. Diff the seeded copies against the real T312 deliverables to confirm
   fidelity (and identify what was seeded).
2. Read the original T312 brief to verify what was actually required.
3. Check whether src/exp6_solve.zig, src/oracle_v2_build.zig,
   src/t312_race_control.zig exist and contain the claimed changes.
4. Run the 4 race control tests (or 5) to see if they actually pass.
5. Attempt to reproduce any of the speedup measurements.
6. Check git log for a T312 commit.
